# 1 Samuel Chapter 1 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 181 | **Source Image:** 1SA_001_page_001.jpg, 1SA_001_page_002.jpg

---

**1** There was a man from Ramathaim-zophim, in the hill country of Ephraim, whose name was Elkanah son of Jeroham, son of Elihu, son of Tohu, son of Zuph — an Ephraimite. **2** He had two wives: one named Hannah, the other Peninnah. Peninnah had children, but Hannah had none.

**3** Every year this man would go up from his town to worship and offer sacrifice to the LORD of Hosts at Shiloh, where Eli's two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, served as priests of the LORD. **4** Whenever the day came for Elkanah to sacrifice, he would give portions to his wife Peninnah and to each of her sons and daughters. **5** But to Hannah he would give a double portion, because he loved her deeply — even though the LORD had closed her womb. **6** And her rival would provoke her relentlessly, taunting her because the LORD had shut her womb. **7** This went on year after year. Every time they went up to the house of the LORD, Peninnah would needle her until she wept and could not eat.

**8** "Hannah," her husband Elkanah said to her, "why are you crying? Why won't you eat? Why are you so downhearted? Am I not worth more to you than ten sons?"

**9** After they had eaten and drunk at Shiloh, Hannah got up. Now Eli the priest was sitting on a seat by the doorpost of the LORD's temple. **10** In deep anguish, Hannah prayed to the LORD, weeping bitterly. **11** She made a vow: "O LORD of Hosts, if you would only look — truly look — at your servant's misery, if you would remember me and not forget me, if you would give your servant a son, then I will give him back to the LORD for all the days of his life, and no razor will ever touch his head."

**12** As she kept praying before the LORD, Eli was watching her mouth. **13** Hannah was praying in her heart; her lips were moving, but no sound came out. So Eli thought she was drunk. **14** "How long are you going to keep this up?" Eli said to her. "Sober up and put the wine away!"

**15** "No, my lord," Hannah answered. "I am a woman crushed in spirit. I haven't had wine or anything strong — I have been pouring out my soul before the LORD. **16** Don't take your servant for some worthless woman. I have been praying out of the depths of my grief and anguish."

**17** "Then go in peace," Eli answered, "and may the God of Israel grant what you have asked of him."

**18** "May your servant find favor in your eyes," she said. Then the woman went on her way, ate something, and her face was no longer downcast.

**19** They rose early the next morning, worshipped before the LORD, and returned home to Ramah. Elkanah was intimate with his wife Hannah, and the LORD remembered her. **20** In the course of time, Hannah conceived and gave birth to a son. She named him Samuel, saying, "Because I asked the LORD for him."

**21** When Elkanah went up with his whole household to offer the annual sacrifice to the LORD and fulfill his vow, **22** Hannah did not go. She told her husband, "Once the boy is weaned, I will bring him to appear before the LORD — and there he will stay permanently." **23** "Do what you think is best," her husband Elkanah told her. "Stay until you have weaned him. May the LORD bring his word to fulfillment." So the woman stayed home and nursed her son until she weaned him.

**24** Once she had weaned him, she took him up with her, along with a three-year-old bull, an ephah of flour, and a skin of wine, and she brought him to the house of the LORD at Shiloh. The boy was still young. **25** They slaughtered the bull and brought the boy to Eli. **26** "Pardon me, my lord," she said. "As surely as you live, my lord, I am the woman who stood here beside you, praying to the LORD. **27** I prayed for this child, and the LORD granted me what I asked of him. **28** So now I am giving him to the LORD. For as long as he lives, he is given over to the LORD." And he worshipped the LORD there.

---

## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**Verse 5 — "double portion":** The Hebrew *manah achat appayim* is notoriously difficult. It may mean "one choice portion" (literally "a portion of the face/presence") or "a double portion." The sense is clear regardless: Elkanah singled Hannah out for special honor because of his love, which made Peninnah's taunting all the more bitter.

**Verse 6 — "needle her":** The Hebrew *ka'as* carries the sense of provoking someone to deep vexation and frustration. I render "needle" to capture the persistent, sharp, personal quality of Peninnah's torment — it was targeted cruelty, not casual rivalry.

**Verse 8 — "Am I not worth more to you than ten sons?":** Elkanah's question is both tender and tone-deaf. He genuinely loves Hannah, but he cannot comprehend that his love does not solve the existential wound of barrenness in her world. I preserve the rhetorical question to let the reader feel the gap.

**Verse 11 — "look — truly look":** The Hebrew uses the infinitive absolute *ra'oh tir'eh* for emphasis — literally "seeing you will see." The doubled verb conveys urgent pleading: *really* see me, don't overlook me.

**Verse 16 — "worthless woman":** Hebrew *bat-beliyya'al*, literally "daughter of worthlessness/destruction." This is a strong social slur. Hannah defends her dignity — she is not some disreputable woman causing a scene.

**Verse 20 — "Samuel" / "asked the LORD":** The name-etymology is a wordplay: *she'iltiv me-YHWH* ("I asked him from the LORD"). The name *Shemu'el* may parse as "heard of God" or "name of God," but the narrator ties it to *sha'al* (to ask). The dynamic rendering preserves the connection between the name and the act of petition.

**Verse 28 — "he is given over to the LORD":** The Hebrew *hu' sha'ul la-YHWH* — "he is lent/dedicated to the LORD" — echoes the wordplay on *sha'al* (to ask) yet again. Hannah asked, and now she gives back. The verb *sha'al* threads through the entire chapter as a literary motif: asking, being granted, being returned.

*— PNEUMA*
